name: Capital A Berhad
oneLine: The group behind the AirAsia brand, whose 2025 accounts split it into the airline business and a set of non-airline businesses such as cargo, aircraft maintenance and a travel app.
inPlainWords: Most people know Capital A through AirAsia flights. In the 2025 accounts the aviation business is shown as a "discontinued operation", separate from the businesses the group continues to run.

The continuing businesses are Teleport (cargo and logistics), ADE (aircraft maintenance and engineering), AirAsia MOVE (online travel and e-commerce app), BigPay (financial services) and AirAsia Next (licensing the AirAsia brand).
In 2025 aviation still made up about 90% of total revenue, so the numbers for the continuing businesses are much smaller than the group most people picture.

flow.label: Passengers
flow.detail: Buy seats and extras on AirAsia flights. Aviation revenue was RM16.5 billion in 2025, shown as a discontinued operation.

flow.label: Cargo customers
flow.detail: Pay Teleport to move freight. RM1.2 billion, the largest continuing business.

flow.label: Airlines
flow.detail: Pay ADE for aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul. RM212 million.

flow.label: App users and brand users
flow.detail: AirAsia MOVE, BigPay and brand licensing fees together brought about RM231 million (calculated).

moneyNote: Read this company's figures with care: the 2025 accounts report continuing businesses (RM1.9 billion revenue) separately from aviation (RM16.5 billion), and the reported profit includes items related to that split.
